Replay

Godot bridge implementation plan

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
InvariantsImplementation sequence and gatesOptimization decisionsValidation and working record

Completed 2026-09-20. See delivery evidence.

This completed plan defined improvements to the API connecting replayable gameplay values and authored Godot scenes, together with measured overhead reductions. It followed the framework-first implementation and required preserving Kit, original games, and separate Replay versions without adding a game-parity campaign.

Implementation and evidence are tracked in bridge progress.

Invariants#

  • Mutable gameplay remains in the replayable World. Godot nodes, input devices, storage and presentation timers stay outside it.
  • Definitions are immutable, validated and versioned. Retain every definition version needed by live history/checkpoints; never hide mutable gameplay behind an asset pointer to reduce copying.
  • Presentation receives detached values with explicit predicted/observed/authority sampling policy. Presentation selection grants no simulation authority.
  • Entity/view identity includes lifetime generation. View reuse cannot retain stale effects, child state or references to a prior entity.
  • Cached property updates require declared ownership of those properties and an explicit invalidation path for external writers.
  • Keep plain APIs usable without codegen. Add generated mapping only after a typed manual mapping demonstrates useful repetition to remove.

Implementation sequence and gates#

Step Shared primitive Acceptance
B1 Bounded indexed identity lookup and opt-in cached node updates Duplicate/invalid input preflight, retained identities and lifecycle replacement; actual Godot properties/resource cleanup; before/after operation counts and representative timings
B2 Typed entity/view pool and small presentation projections Typed project/paint callbacks, generation-safe views, cached child bindings, explicit sampling/teleports; rewind spawn/death in one small game without changing World hashes
B3 Resource/scene definition baking Typed bounded values, stable content identities, useful field/path errors, atomic rejection, resource ownership and retained-version rules; one existing authored level/resource integration
B4 Input/signal bindings over Controls and Action_Intent Tick-edge capture, pause/focus/menu policy, submission retry and epoch-scoped outcomes; no direct UI mutation of World and no ambiguous click queue
B5 Declarative visual/audio effect routes Existing journal IDs/policies, bounded pools, update/confirm without restart, cancel and lifetime reuse; native/WASM and focused actual-engine checks
B6 Explicit simulation-driven and cooperative body bindings Authored transform ownership, authority-gated observations, freeze/reseed/transfer/correction; no claim that Godot physics becomes deterministic
B7 Measured optimization and delivery Compare representative lookup/property/copy/encoding/replay costs; implement justified improvements, document public APIs and remaining limits, maintain compile-checked examples

The plan started with B1/B2 because the original Nodes2 implementation repeatedly scanned arrays and applied all four properties on every presentation call. Preserve its default behavior for existing games; higher-level bindings can opt into property caching. Current scene/resource extraction, input latches, cues, Audio_Pool and Body2/Body3 are implementation foundations, not functionality to rewrite under new names.

Optimization decisions#

First measure indexed lookup, skipped Godot calls and small detached projections. Then identify immutable data that can safely leave history, and repeated canonical encoding/hashing that can be shared without crossing recipient privacy boundaries. Existing exact correction reuse remains opt-in and must retain full dependencies.

Evaluate chunked/copy-on-write history only if representative profiles show a remaining storage/copy bottleneck. Ordinary gameplay assignments are a central benefit; do not introduce mandatory mutation APIs merely to make dirty tracking easy. Document a decision to defer this optimization when evidence does not justify its complexity; do not report an unimplemented optimization as a speedup.

Validation and working record#

Use focused pure/native/WASM tests and one or two existing examples to exercise each boundary. Reuse existing recovery and journal contracts. No full-game parity matrix is required. Record changed sources, relevant logs, exact workload and measurement limitations; avoid duplicating the whole repository per increment. B1–B7's required behavior and evidence are complete; see the linked delivery assessment.
